title: Stability and diagonal of an ind-etale algebra
statement:
The classes of ind-etale [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra] and ind-Zariski
maps are stable under base change, composition, and filtered colimits. An
ind-etale map is weakly etale. If $B,C$ are ind-etale over $A$, every
$A$-algebra map $B\to C$ is ind-etale. Weakly etale maps are stable under
composition and base change.

proof.text: Reuse the fully proved source-library results RingHom.IndEtale.isStableUnderBaseChange and RingHom.IndEtale.comp for ind-etale base change and composition. RingHom.IndEtale.weaklyEtale gives weak etaleness. For an A-algebra map f : B -> C between ind-etale A-algebras, f composed with algebraMap A B equals algebraMap A C by f.commutes, so RingHom.IndEtale.of_comp proves f ind-etale. No affine etale-descent or idempotent-splitting obligation is needed here.

source.place: Proof, paragraphs 1-2; existing source-library ind-etale APIs

proof.text: Let blocks A be the property of being isomorphic as an A-algebra to a finite product of principal localizations. Construct tensorBlockEquiv using Algebra.TensorProduct.piRight and IsLocalization.algEquiv: S tensor_A product_j A_(f_j) is product_j S_(image f_j), including the empty product. Realize algebra base change as the equivalence with Under A, pushout along A -> S, and the inverse equivalence with S-algebras. This functor preserves colimits and has the explicit tensor-product equivalence bcEquiv. Map the filtered block presentation through it and transport across bcEquiv. Algebra.IsPushout.equiv then gives stability under arbitrary base-change squares.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 1: explicit tensor and colimit base change

proof.text: Regard blocks as the morphism property blockMaps on CommRingCat. The equivalence between A-algebras and Under A, together with ObjectProperty.ind_inverseImage_eq_of_isEquivalence, identifies the given principal ind-Zariski definition with blockMaps.ind. Every block is etale: principal localizations are etale and finite products preserve etaleness. Hence every block is finitely presented and CommRingCat.isFinitelyPresentable_under gives blockMaps <= MorphismProperty.isFinitelyPresentable. MorphismProperty.ind_ind then shows that ind of principal ind-Zariski is principal ind-Zariski.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 1: finite blocks and flattening filtered presentations

proof.text: Prove blocks closed under composition. A principal localization of a finite product is the product of the localized factors, by IsLocalization.iff_map_piEvalRingHom. For g in A_f choose its numerator a with IsLocalization.Away.sec; IsLocalization.Away.mul_of_associated identifies (A_f)_g with A_(f*a). Flatten a finite product of finite products using a dependent finite index and Fintype.equivFin. These arguments also cover the empty product and zero localizations. Prove blocks spread over filtered colimits by choosing representatives of their finitely many denominators at one common stage, using Concrete.isColimit_exists_rep and a cocone over a finite discrete diagram. The explicit tensorBlockEquiv supplies the required pushout. Apply the already proved source theorem MorphismProperty.IsStableUnderComposition.ind_of_le_isFinitelyPresentable to blockMaps and its finite-presentation bound, composition, cobase-change and PreIndSpreads instances. Transfer the result through principal_iff_ind.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 1: composition and finite denominator descent

proof.text: Prove the varying-base filtered-colimit step directly by universal properties. Given a filtered diagram of stage arrows F_i -> G_i and colimit source A and target B, set E_i = A pushout_(F_i) G_i. Pushout descent gives the transition maps. The maps from A into any cocone over E are independent of the index, since filteredness gives a common receiving index. From the G colimit obtain the unique map out of B, and use the F colimit and pushout hom-extensionality to prove its compatibility with E_i and uniqueness. Thus B is the colimit of E. If P is stable under cobase change and each stage arrow lies in P, every A -> E_i lies in P and hence A -> B lies in P.ind. Apply this construction first to ind-etale maps and use RingHom.IndEtale.iff_ind_indEtale; apply it again to principal ind-Zariski maps and use the flattening identity of step 3. Arrow.leftFunc and Arrow.rightFunc preserve the given arrow-category colimit.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 1: filtered colimits with varying source rings

proof.text: Reuse RingHom.WeaklyEtale.comp for composition. For base change, RingHom.IsStableUnderBaseChange.mk reduces to invariance under ring isomorphism and the canonical tensor-product square. Composition with bijective maps proves the former, since a bijective ring map is etale and hence weakly etale. The latter is exactly the existing Algebra.WeaklyEtale tensor-product instance after rewriting RingHom.weaklyEtale_algebraMap_iff. Assemble the ten clauses in their original order.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 3: existing weakly etale composition and tensor-product APIs

lean.statement: theorem indEtale_principalZariski_stability : RingHom.IsStableUnderBaseChange (@RingHom.IndEtale.{u}) ∧ RingHom.IsStableUnderBaseChange (fun {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] (f : A →+* B) ↦ @Algebra.IsIndPrincipalZariski A B _ _ f.toAlgebra) ∧ RingHom.StableUnderComposition (@RingHom.IndEtale.{u}) ∧ RingHom.StableUnderComposition (fun {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] (f : A →+* B) ↦ @Algebra.IsIndPrincipalZariski A B _ _ f.toAlgebra) ∧ (∀ (I : Type u) [SmallCategory I] [IsFiltered I] (D : I ⥤ Arrow CommRingCat.{u}) (c : Cocone D), IsColimit c → (∀ i : I, (D.obj i).hom.hom.IndEtale) → c.pt.hom.hom.IndEtale) ∧ (∀ (I : Type u) [SmallCategory I] [IsFiltered I] (D : I ⥤ Arrow CommRingCat.{u}) (c : Cocone D), IsColimit c → (∀ i : I, @Algebra.IsIndPrincipalZariski (D.obj i).left (D.obj i).right _ _ (D.obj i).hom.hom.toAlgebra) → @Algebra.IsIndPrincipalZariski c.pt.left c.pt.right _ _ c.pt.hom.hom.toAlgebra) ∧ (∀ (A B : Type u) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] (f : A →+* B), f.IndEtale → f.WeaklyEtale) ∧ (∀ (A B C : Type u) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [CommRing C] [Algebra A B] [Algebra A C], Algebra.IndEtale A B → Algebra.IndEtale A C → ∀ f : B →ₐ[A] C, f.toRingHom.IndEtale) ∧ RingHom.StableUnderComposition (@RingHom.WeaklyEtale.{u, u}) ∧ RingHom.IsStableUnderBaseChange (@RingHom.WeaklyEtale.{u, u})
